title: Response to province on Regional Official Plan
subtitle: Uptown rental conversion at 180 King Street South, Eby Farm options report, and annual committee reports.
overview: Council directed the Mayor to tell the Province that Waterloo supports the Regional Official Plan as approved by Regional Council in August 2022, with no changes. The response also reaffirms the Countryside Line, intensification and the pledge to build 16,000 housing units by 2031. It asks that official plan decisions be made by all of Council with public input, not by heads of council alone {{vote:m10}}.

Council approved a rezoning for 180 King Street South in Uptown. It allows a purpose-built rental conversion of the existing Allen Square office building, with added storeys and a one-storey podium, up to 40 metres {{vote:m8}}. Council also asked staff to report in the new year on options for the future of Eby Farm in Waterloo Park {{vote:m2}}.

The evening was also the annual committee night. Council heard from advisory committees on town and gown relations, active transportation, sustainability, economic development, age-friendly planning, parks and accessibility, and received the annual reports as information. A strategic plan presentation opened the session. A formal public meeting for a University of Waterloo rezoning at 155 University Avenue West was deferred.

decisions.item: Response to Minister on Regional Official Plan
decisions.detail: Council directed the Mayor to submit feedback by December 7, 2023 supporting the Regional Official Plan as approved in August 2022, the Countryside Line, and the 16,000-unit housing pledge {{vote:m10}}.
Council approved Z-23-05 allowing a 40-metre, 10-storey building, with flexibility for two-storey top units or a mezzanine, and a minimum podium height of 4.6 metres {{vote:m8}}.
Council directed staff to return in the new year with a report on options for the future of Eby Farm {{vote:m2}}.
Council waived the notice requirement so the Mayor's response to the Minister's letter could be considered at this meeting {{vote:m9}}.
Council received the 2023 Community Grants Committee report as information {{vote:m6}}.

debate: On the provincial letter, one councillor and the Mayor said that giving only heads of council a say on adding land to the Regional Official Plan erodes local democracy. They noted the 2022 plan followed extensive public consultation.

Speakers argued the Regional Official Plan already provides enough land to meet housing targets, and that the Countryside Line protects farmland, water recharge areas and the region's urban-rural character.

On 180 King Street South, a delegate speaking for a group of nearby residents supported adaptive reuse but objected to the south-side podium. They said it would reduce the side-yard setback and endanger mature trees on Allen Street.

Staff replied that the reduced setback reflects the existing underground parking structure and that the building design was revised to protect the trees. The applicant's planners said the City-owned trees are to be kept, with the work done on top of the existing parking deck, so no new excavation is needed.

Councillors also asked about parking, sanitary sewer capacity downstream, school bus conflicts during construction, and accessible units. Staff and the applicant said parking is existing, capacity is available with a flag for later review, a construction staging plan is required, and accessible units will exceed the minimum.
On Eby Farm, one councillor asked staff to clarify what the report should cover. The Mayor said all options should be on the table, and staff said public input would follow after the report.
